mainTopic: Night travel for a תלמיד חכם, aggadot about יעקב, and the angels' שירה
overview: The amud opens with the end of a list of פסוקים that teach one rule: a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night. The proofs come from בועז, אברהם, יעקב sending יוסף, and יעקב waiting for sunrise. That last פסוק, 'ויזרח לו השמש', leads רבי עקיבא to ask why the sun rose 'for him'. רבי יצחק answers that the sun had once set early just for יעקב, at the place where he went back to pray. The גמרא then retells that night: the stones that merged into one, the huge ladder with its angels, ה׳ standing over יעקב to protect him, and all of ארץ ישראל folded under him. Next it returns to יעקב wrestling the מלאך, who had to leave at dawn because his turn to sing had finally come. This supports רב's teaching that three groups of angels share the daily שירה. A ברייתא saying angels mention ה׳'s Name only after three words forces the גמרא to fix רב's wording. The amud ends with a new challenge from the angels' praise 'ברוך כבוד ה׳', where the Name comes after only two words.

steps.title: בועז stayed overnight at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק about בועז that serves as a source that a תלמיד חכם does not go out alone at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Behold, he winnows the barley at the threshing floor" (tonight).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started just before this section. The פסוק shows that בועז stayed at the threshing floor at night instead of walking home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעמי tells רות that בועז is winnowing barley that night and will lie down there. Why did he sleep at the threshing floor instead of going home? Because a תלמיד חכם like בועז should not walk out alone at night.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar, the person this whole rule is about
Winnows (tosses grain in the wind to separate it from the chaff)
Threshing floor, an open area outside town where grain is processed

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a list. The rule itself (a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night) and the name of whoever brought this פסוק came just before. Here we only see the end of that proof.

phrases.english: "Behold, he winnows
phrases.notes: רות 3:2. נעמי is speaking to רות about בועז.

phrases.english: the barley at the threshing floor."

steps.triggerLanguage: הִנֵּה הוּא זֹרֶה אֶת גֹּרֶן הַשְּׂעֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source brought just before this section for the rule that a תלמיד חכם does not go out alone at night.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: רות 3:2–3: בועז spends the night at the threshing floor rather than returning home

steps.title: רבי אבהו's source: אברהם waited until morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a different source: אברהם got up early in the morning to travel, and did not set out at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: the source is from here: "And אברהם rose early in the morning and saddled" his donkey, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו offers his own פסוק as the source for the same rule. אברהם waited for morning before setting out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was eager to do what ה׳ commanded, yet he still waited until morning instead of leaving at night. He was not even alone, since he took two young men and יצחק with him. That suggests a תלמיד חכם should avoid traveling at night, and certainly alone.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning this פסוק is the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: from here:
"And Avraham rose early in the morning
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:3, as אברהם sets out for the עקדה.

phrases.english: and saddled, etc."
phrases.notes: "וגו׳" means "and so on." The פסוק continues: his donkey, and took two young men and יצחק with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule proven in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 22:3: אברהם set out only in the morning

steps.title: רבנן's source: יעקב sent יוסף by day
steps.stepSummary: רבנן bring a source from יעקב sending יוסף to "see" how his brothers were doing, which implies daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן say: the source is from here: "Go now, see how your brothers are doing and how the flock is doing," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן offer a third פסוק for the same rule. יעקב sent יוסף at a time when he could "see," meaning during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "see" (ראה) hints that יוסף traveled while it was light enough to see. So יעקב made sure his son did not set out alone at night. This again teaches that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night.

keyTerms.meaning: See, the key word that hints at daylight

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: from here:
"Go now, see the welfare of your brothers
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:14. יעקב is speaking to יוסף.

phrases.english: and the welfare of, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative פסוק for the same rule, after רבי אבהו's.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 37:14: "see" implies יוסף was sent during daylight

steps.title: רב's source: יעקב left only when the sun rose
steps.stepSummary: רב brings a source from יעקב after his struggle with the angel: he set out only once the sun had risen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the source is from here: "And the sun rose for him."
steps.whatsHappening: רב offers a fourth פסוק for the same rule. יעקב, who was alone, waited until sunrise before moving on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the sun rose for יעקב as he passed פנואל. That means he stayed where he was through the night and traveled only in daylight. A תלמיד חכם who is alone should likewise not travel at night.
steps.whatToRemember: All these opinions agree on one rule: a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night. They differ only about which פסוק is the source: בועז, אברהם, יעקב sending יוסף, or יעקב waiting for sunrise.

phrases.english: Rav said: from here:
"And the sun rose for him."
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:32, right after יעקב wrestled with the angel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last alternative פסוק in the list for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 32:32: יעקב moved on only once the sun rose

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks why the sun shone only 'for him'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tells how he asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע why the פסוק says the sun shone 'for' יעקב, when the sun shines for the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע in the meat market of אימאום, when they went to buy an animal for the wedding feast of רבן גמליאל's son. It says, 'And the sun shone for him.' Did the sun shine only for him? It shone for the whole world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the פסוק from step 4, 'ויזרח לו השמש', and raises a question about the word 'לו' (for him). This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun rises for everyone, so the word 'לו' seems unneeded. רבי עקיבא's question assumes that every word in the פסוק must teach something. The story setting simply shows where and when he asked.

keyTerms.meaning: A meat market, where animals were sold
A feast, here a wedding feast
'And the sun shone for him', the פסוק about יעקב after he wrestled the angel
'But isn't it so...', which opens a strong question

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: I asked

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְאֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua
in the meat market of Emmaus,
where they went to buy an animal
for the feast of Rabban Gamliel's son.
It is written: "And the sun shone for him,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:32, the same פסוק רב used in step 4.

phrases.english: But did the sun shine only for him?
Didn't it shine for the whole world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק quoted in step 4 and asks about its unusual wording
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says the sun shone 'for him' when the sun shines for everyone

steps.title: The sun that set for him rose for him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the sun once set early just for יעקב, so later it rose early just for him to balance it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The sun that set for his sake shone for his sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers רבי עקיבא's question: the sun rose 'for him' because it had earlier set early 'for him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לו' points to a special event made just for יעקב. Since the sun once set early for his sake, it rose early for his sake to make up the lost time. The next steps show when that early sunset happened.

keyTerms.meaning: For his sake, because of him
Here it means 'that set', from 'בא השמש'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The sun that set for his sake
phrases.notes: 'בָּאָה' here means 'set', like the פסוק 'בָּא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ' that comes later.

phrases.english: shone for his sake,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לו' means the sun rose early for יעקב to balance the earlier time it set early for him

steps.title: The land jumps so יעקב can return to pray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings פסוקים to show the background: יעקב reached חרן, realized he had passed the place where his fathers prayed, and the land shrank so he arrived there right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And יעקב went out from באר שבע and went toward חרן,' and it says: 'And he encountered the place.' When he reached חרן he said: Is it possible that I passed a place where my fathers prayed and I did not pray? When he decided to go back, the land jumped for him, and right away, 'And he encountered the place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story behind the early sunset, using the פסוקים in בראשית about יעקב's trip to חרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יעקב already went to חרן, yet then says he 'encountered the place'. רבי יצחק reads this as a return trip: he went back to pray where his fathers prayed, and the land miraculously shrank so he arrived immediately. This sets up the next step, where the sun sets early.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he encountered the place', meaning he came upon the place where his fathers prayed
The land jumped (shrank) for him, so a long trip became instant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ויפגע במקום' as happening on the way to חרן. In this telling, יעקב had already reached חרן and then went back to the place.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:10

phrases.english: and went toward Charan,"
And it is written: "And he encountered the place."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:11

phrases.english: When he reached Charan, he said:
Is it possible that I passed a place
where my fathers prayed, and I did not pray?
When he made up his mind to go back,
the land jumped for him,
phrases.notes: The distance shrank, so he got there right away.

phrases.english: immediately: "And he encountered the place."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing from the פסוקים when the sun set early for יעקב
steps.raayaObject: That there was a special early sunset for יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 28:10-11, read as יעקב returning from חרן to the place of prayer

steps.title: God makes the sun set early so יעקב stays
steps.stepSummary: After יעקב prayed and wanted to leave, הקדוש ברוך הוא made the sun set early so the צדיק would stay the night at His 'lodging place'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he prayed, he wanted to go back. הקדוש ברוך הוא said: This צדיק came to My lodging place, and he will leave without staying the night? Right away, 'the sun set.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story and shows the exact moment the sun set early just for יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כי בא השמש', and רבי יצחק reads it as an early sunset made for יעקב so he would sleep there. This completes the answer from step 6: that early sunset is why the sun later rose early 'for him'.

keyTerms.meaning: My lodging place, meaning the holy place of prayer

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק: the sun set early for יעקב so he would sleep at the holy place, and so it rose early for him later. That is the meaning of 'ויזרח לו השמש'.

phrases.english: When he prayed, he wanted to go back;
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
This righteous man came to My lodging place,
and he will leave without staying the night?
Immediately, "the sun set."
phrases.notes: So the sun went down before its normal time. This is the early sunset רבי יצחק mentioned in step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun in step 7 and pinpoints the early sunset
steps.raayaObject: The early sunset that was 'for him'

steps.title: Stones or one stone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק says יעקב took 'from the stones' (many), while a later one says he took 'the stone' (one).
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'And he took from the stones of the place,' and it says: 'And he took the stone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices two פסוקים in the same story that seem to clash. It is setting up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night יעקב took several stones, but in the morning the פסוק speaks of just one stone. How did many stones become one?

keyTerms.meaning: From the stones of the place, which sounds like many stones

phrases.english: It is written: "And he took from the stones of the place,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:11

phrases.english: And it is written: "And he took the stone."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:18

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״וַיִּקַּח מֵאַבְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם״, וּכְתִיב ״וַיִּקַּח אֶת הָאֶבֶן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the same night in יעקב's story but raises a new question about the stones
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים describing the stones יעקב used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק implies many stones and the other implies one stone

steps.title: The stones gathered, each wanting the צדיק's head
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that all the stones gathered into one spot, and each one asked that the צדיק rest his head on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: This teaches that all those stones gathered to one place, and each one said: 'Let this צדיק rest his head on me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק begins resolving the contradiction by telling what happened to the many stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'many stones' were real, but they all crowded into one spot because each wanted the honor of holding the צדיק's head. This explains how the stones came together. The next line explains how they became one.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches, introducing a lesson learned from the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: This teaches

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ כׇּל אוֹתָן אֲבָנִים לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that all those stones gathered to one place,
and each and every one said:
"Let this righteous man rest his head on me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ כׇּל אוֹתָן אֲבָנִים לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both פסוקים are true at different moments: many stones that came together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים disagree about how many stones there were
steps.terutzMaskana: There were many stones, and they all gathered to one place out of love for the צדיק

steps.title: All the stones merged into one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that all the stones were absorbed into a single stone, which is why the later פסוק says 'the stone'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And all of them were swallowed up into one.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא finishes the answer: the many stones became one stone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק explained why the stones gathered, and this line explains how 'many' became 'one'. Now both פסוקים fit: at night many stones, in the morning one stone.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Stones' became 'the stone' because all the stones gathered for the צדיק and merged into one.

phrases.english: It was taught: And they were all swallowed up into one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יצחק's answer with a ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The many stones merged into one stone, which settles the contradiction between 'stones' and 'the stone'

steps.title: How wide was the ladder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק of יעקב's dream, and a ברייתא asks how wide the ladder was.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth." A ברייתא taught: How wide was the ladder?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next פסוק in the story, יעקב's dream. A ברייתא asks a question about the ladder's width, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says nothing about how wide the ladder was. The ברייתא asks because it is about to work out a number from details in other פסוקים.

phrases.english: "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth"
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:12

phrases.english: It was taught: How wide was the ladder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the stones (steps 9-11) to the dream itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The width of the ladder in יעקב's dream.

steps.title: Eight thousand parasangs, because four angels fit on it
steps.stepSummary: The answer is 8,000 פרסאות. The plural words 'ascending' and 'descending' show two angels going up and two going down, so four angels were side by side when they met.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eight thousand parasangs, as it is written: "And behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it." "Ascending" means two, "descending" means two, and when they met each other there were four.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the ladder was 8,000 פרסאות wide. It begins its proof by showing that four angels stood side by side on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words עולים and יורדים are plural, and the smallest plural is two. So two angels went up and two came down. When they passed each other, the ladder had to hold four angels side by side. This is only the first half of the proof; the next step gives the size of each angel.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs, a long measure of distance

phrases.english: Eight thousand parasangs,
as it is written: "And behold the angels of God
ascending and descending on it"
"Ascending" means two, "and descending" means two,
phrases.notes: A plural word means at least two, so the ברייתא counts two angels in each direction.

phrases.english: and when they met one another
they were four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 8,000 פרסאות, starting with the fact that four angels stood side by side on the ladder.

steps.title: Each angel is the size of תרשיש
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says an angel's body is like תרשיש, and there is a tradition that תרשיש is 2,000 פרסאות. Four angels × 2,000 = 8,000.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written about an angel: "His body was like תרשיש," and we have a tradition that תרשיש is two thousand פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its proof by giving the size of one angel. Four angels of 2,000 פרסאות each makes 8,000.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave the number of angels (four). This step gives the size of each one, using a פסוק in דניאל plus a known tradition about תרשיש. Put together, they make the full 8,000 figure.

keyTerms.meaning: Tarshish, a place known by tradition to be 2,000 פרסאות
We have it as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: Two plural words make four angels, and each angel is 2,000 פרסאות, so the ladder was 8,000 פרסאות wide.

phrases.english: And it is written about an angel:
"His body was like Tarshish,"
phrases.notes: דניאל 10:6

phrases.english: and we have a tradition that Tarshish
is two thousand parasangs.
phrases.notes: Four angels at 2,000 each comes to the 8,000 the ברייתא started with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the math begun in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the ladder was 8,000 פרסאות wide.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דניאל 10:6 (an angel's body like תרשיש) plus the tradition that תרשיש is 2,000 פרסאות.

steps.title: The angels look at יעקב's image, and ה׳ protects him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the angels went up and looked at יעקב's image above, then came down and looked at him below. They wanted to harm him, and right away ה׳ stood over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They would go up and look at his image above, and come down and look at his image below. They wanted to endanger him. Immediately: "And behold, God stood over him."
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא explains why the angels were going up and down. They were comparing יעקב's image in heaven to יעקב on earth, wanted to harm him, and ה׳ stepped in to protect him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reads the next פסוק, 'ה׳ stood over him,' as a reaction to danger. עליו is read as 'over יעקב,' protecting him, and not just 'over the ladder.'

phrases.english: It was taught: They would go up and gaze
at his image above,
phrases.notes: "His" means יעקב. His image was up in heaven.

phrases.english: and come down and gaze at his image below.
They wanted to endanger him,
immediately: "And behold, God stood over him."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:13

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: עוֹלִין וּמִסְתַּכְּלִין בִּדְיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ladder's size to what the angels on it were doing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels compared יעקב above and below, wanted to harm him, and ה׳ stood over him to protect him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: like a father fanning his son
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that without the פסוק we could never say it, but ה׳ stood over יעקב like a man waving over his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: If the verse were not written, it would be impossible to say it: like a man who waves over his son.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds a comment on the words 'ה׳ stood over him.' He compares it to a father waving a fan over his child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Describing ה׳ as standing over a person like a caring father is very bold. ריש לקיש says we may say it only because the פסוק itself says it.

keyTerms.meaning: If the verse were not written
It would be impossible to say it

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ guarded יעקב with a father's closeness, and ריש לקיש says only the פסוק allows us to describe it this way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Were it not a written verse,
it would be impossible to say it,
like a man who waves over his son.
phrases.notes: Picture a father fanning his child to cool and protect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאׇמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the פסוק quoted at the end of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ה׳ stood over him' means ה׳ protected יעקב like a father fanning his son. We may say this only because the פסוק says it.

steps.title: Why promise 'the land you lie on'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the promise 'the land on which you lie' and asks what is so great about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The land on which you lie, etc." What is its greatness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the wording of ה׳'s promise to יעקב. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was lying on only a small spot of ground. A promise of just that spot seems tiny, so the גמרא asks why the פסוק phrases the promise this way.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its greatness? What is special about it?

phrases.english: "The land on which you lie, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:13

phrases.english: What is its greatness?
phrases.notes: He was lying on a small patch of ground, so what kind of big promise is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק (28:13).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the promise is worded as 'the land on which you lie' when that was such a small area.

steps.title: All of ארץ ישראל was folded under יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that הקדוש ברוך הוא folded up all of ארץ ישראל and put it under יעקב, so it would be easy for his children to conquer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא folded up all of ארץ ישראל and placed it under יעקב אבינו, so that it would be easy for his children to conquer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question of step 17. יעקב was lying on all of ארץ ישראל, folded up beneath him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the spot under יעקב was small. רבי יצחק answers that it was not small at all, since the whole land was folded under him. That way 'the land you lie on' means the entire land, and this made it easier for his descendants to conquer it.
steps.whatToRemember: 'The land on which you lie' means all of ארץ ישראל, which ה׳ folded under יעקב so his children could conquer it easily.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: This teaches
that the Holy One, Blessed be He, folded up
all of the Land of Israel
and placed it under Yaakov our father,
so that it would be easy for his children to conquer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁקִּפְּלָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ folded all of ארץ ישראל under יעקב, so 'the land you lie on' is the whole land, and this made it easy for his children to conquer.

steps.title: The angel asks to leave at dawn, and יעקב asks why
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the מלאך asked to be let go because dawn had come. יעקב asks him if he is a thief or a gambler who is afraid of daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he said: Let me go, for the dawn has risen.' יעקב said to him: Are you a thief, or a gambler, that you are afraid of the dawn?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of יעקב wrestling with the מלאך and quotes the next פסוק. יעקב asks why the מלאך is in such a hurry to leave when morning comes. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who do shady things at night, like thieves and gamblers, are afraid of being seen in daylight. יעקב is asking why a being like this would care about the sun coming up. The question prepares the מלאך's surprising answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me go / send me away
Dawn has risen; morning has come

phrases.english: "And he said: Let me go, for the dawn has risen."
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:27

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you a thief
or are you a gambler,
phrases.notes: A קוביוסטוס is someone who plays dice for money.

phrases.english: that you are afraid of the dawn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ladder dream (steps 12–18) and goes back to יעקב wrestling the מלאך (בראשית 32), the episode of 'ויזרח לו השמש' from steps 4–5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the מלאך afraid of dawn and in a hurry to leave?

steps.title: The angel explains: his turn to sing has finally come
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך answers that he is an angel, and since he was created his time to sing שירה to ה׳ has never come until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am an angel, and from the day I was created, my time to say שירה has not come until now.
steps.whatsHappening: The מלאך answers יעקב's question. He has to go because this is the first time ever that his turn has come to sing praise to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלאך's hurry has nothing to do with fear of being seen. He is waiting for a very rare moment, his turn to sing. This shows that a single angel may wait a very long time for his turn, which the גמרא will use in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am an angel,
and from the day I was created
my time to say a song has not arrived
until now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers יעקב's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He must leave because his turn to sing שירה has come for the first time since he was created.

steps.title: This supports רב: three groups of angels share the song
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the story supports רב חננאל in the name of רב. He taught that three groups of angels sing every day, each saying a part of 'קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳ צבאות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports what רב חננאל said in the name of רב. For רב חננאל said in the name of רב: Three groups of מלאכי השרת say שירה every day. One says 'קדוש', another says 'קדוש', and another says 'קדוש ה׳ צבאות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a teaching of רב. Since the singing is split among groups, it makes sense that one angel could wait a long time for his turn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that the angels do not all sing everything together. The song is divided among different groups. The story of the angel who waited from creation fits well with this picture of taking turns.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy, the words of the angels' song in ישעיהו

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: This supports Rav Chananel quoting Rav,
for Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
Three groups of ministering angels
say a song every day:
one says "Holy,"
and another says "Holy,"
and another says "Holy is the Lord of hosts."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 6:3

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the angel's answer as support for a teaching of רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that three groups of angels divide the daily שירה among them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the angel whose turn to sing came only at dawn with יעקב.

steps.title: Objection from a ברייתא: ישראל sing more often than angels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying ישראל are dearer to ה׳ than the angels. ישראל may sing at any time, while angels sing only once a day, or even less often.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: ישראל are dearer to הקדוש ברוך הוא than the מלאכי השרת. ישראל say שירה at any time, but the angels say שירה only once a day. Some say once a week, some say once a month, some say once a year, some say once in seven years, some say once in a יובל, and some say once in the whole history of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to challenge רב's teaching. This is the setup; the exact point that clashes with רב comes in the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists many opinions about how rarely angels sing, from once a day down to once in all of history. The point is that ישראל have a special closeness to ה׳, since they may praise Him anytime. The next lines add a detail about the Name that will press against רב's words.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: The Jewish people are dear before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
more than the ministering angels,
for the Jewish people say a song at any time,
but the ministering angels do not say a song
except once a day,
and some say once a week,
phrases.notes: Here שבת means a whole week, not just the day of שבת.

phrases.english: and some say once a month,
and some say once a year,
and some say once in seven years,
phrases.notes: Here שבוע means a seven-year cycle, like the שמיטה cycle, not a week.

phrases.english: and some say once in a Jubilee,
and some say once in the whole world.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to challenge רב's teaching from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חננאל in the name of רב: three groups of angels sing every day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes the angels' singing as limited and rare compared to ישראל. The specific clash with רב's wording is spelled out in the next part of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that ישראל say ה׳'s Name after two words, as in 'שמע ישראל ה׳', but the angels say it only after three words, 'קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ישראל mention the Name after two words, as it says: 'שמע ישראל ה׳'. But the מלאכי השרת mention the Name only after three words, as it is written: 'קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳ צבאות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second sign that ישראל are dearer than the angels. ישראל may say ה׳'s Name sooner than the angels may.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line seems to be where the challenge to רב lands. רב said one group of angels says 'קדוש ה׳ צבאות', saying the Name after only one word. But the ברייתא says angels never say the Name before three words.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the counting. In 'שמע ישראל ה׳' the Name is the third word, after two words. In 'קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳' it is the fourth word, after three words. רב's group saying 'קדוש ה׳' would be saying the Name after just one word.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא praises ישראל over the angels in two ways: they may sing anytime, and they say ה׳'s Name after two words, while the angels wait for three. This seems to clash with רב's angel group that says 'קדוש ה׳ צבאות'.

phrases.english: And the Jewish people mention the Name
after two words,
as it is stated: "Hear, Israel: The Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.aramaic: וּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אֵין מַזְכִּירִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם
phrases.english: but the ministering angels do not mention the Name
except after three words,
as it is written: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 6:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַזְכִּירִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא begun in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that one group of angels says 'קדוש ה׳ צבאות'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If angels only say the Name after three words, no group of angels could say 'קדוש ה׳' with the Name after a single word.

steps.title: The angels may not sing until ישראל sing first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a third point. The מלאכי השרת do not sing above until ישראל sing below. The proof is a פסוק in איוב where the morning stars (ישראל) sing first, and only afterward the sons of God (the angels) shout for joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ministering angels do not sing above until ישראל sing below, as it says: 'When the morning stars sang together,' and only after that, 'And all the sons of God shouted for joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא from the last two steps. It adds one more way ישראל come before the angels: the angels must wait for ישראל to sing first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts ישראל, called 'morning stars', before the angels, called 'sons of God', so ישראל's song comes first. Together with step 23, this ברייתא now clashes with רב חננאל's teaching from step 21. In that teaching one group of angels said ה׳'s Name after fewer than three words, but the ברייתא says angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words.

keyTerms.meaning: The ministering angels who serve ה׳
Morning stars. Here this means ישראל
Sons of God. Here this means the angels

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: And the ministering angels do not sing their song above
until the Jewish people sing below,
as it says: "When the morning stars sang together,"
phrases.notes: איוב 38:7. The 'morning stars' here are ישראל.

phrases.english: and only afterward: "And all the sons of God shouted for joy."
phrases.notes: The 'sons of God' are the angels. They come second in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from steps 22 and 23 with a third point.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חננאל's teaching in the name of רב (step 21) about how the three groups of angels sing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא as a whole says angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words. In רב's version, one group said ה׳'s Name sooner.
steps.whyThisMatters: Finishing the ברייתא sets up the clash that the גמרא solves in the next step by fixing רב's wording.

steps.title: Fixing the wording of רב's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רב's statement. One group says 'קדוש', another says 'קדוש קדוש', and the third says all of 'קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳ צבאות'. Now the angels always say ה׳'s Name after three words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: one group says 'Holy,' one says 'Holy, holy,' and one says 'Holy, holy, holy is ה׳ of hosts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the clash with the ברייתא by fixing how רב's teaching should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, the third group said ה׳'s Name after only one 'קדוש'. In the fixed version, the third group says all three 'קדוש' and only then ה׳'s Name. This matches the ברייתא's rule that angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Here it shows the גמרא is fixing the earlier wording
ה׳ of hosts (one of ה׳'s Names)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never says the question out loud. The word אלא tells you it is fixing רב's earlier wording because it did not fit the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, one group says "Holy,"
phrases.notes: The גמרא is fixing the wording of רב's teaching from step 21.

phrases.english: and another group says "Holy, holy,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
phrases.english: and another group says "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash created by the ברייתא in steps 22 to 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of an earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The third group of angels said ה׳'s Name after only one 'קדוש'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The third group says all three 'קדוש' before ה׳'s Name, so the angels always say it after three words.
steps.whatToRemember: After the fix, רב's teaching matches the ברייתא: angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words.

steps.title: A challenge from the angels' praise 'ברוך כבוד ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule. The angels also say 'ברוך כבוד ה׳', and there ה׳'s Name comes after only two words.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the angels' praise 'Blessed'! ('Blessed be the glory of ה׳', where ה׳'s Name comes after just two words.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the ברייתא's claim that angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל the angels say 'ברוך כבוד ה׳', and ה׳'s Name is the third word, right after two words. That looks just like ישראל's 'שמע ישראל ה׳'. So it seems the ברייתא's difference between ישראל and the angels does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is. Used to bring a case that seems to contradict what was just said
Blessed. This is the start of the angels' praise in יחזקאל

phrases.english: But there is "Blessed"!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 3:12: 'ברוך כבוד ה׳'. Here the angels say ה׳'s Name after only two words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing רב's wording, the גמרא now attacks the ברייתא's rule itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule (step 23) that angels say ה׳'s Name only after three words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the angels' praise 'ברוך כבוד ה׳', ה׳'s Name comes after only two words, which goes against the ברייתא's rule.
